cues.en: For better or for worse, English is the most important language in modern humanity for international
cues.zh: 無論好壞，英文是現代人類國際

cues.en: collaborations, and this is also reflected in language models.
cues.zh: 合作最重要的語言，這也反映在語言模型中。

cues.en: The most popular language models come from the US, and their training has been dominated by English language texts.
cues.zh: 最受歡迎的語言模型來自美國，訓練文字以英文為主。

cues.en: Now, partly that reflects the fact that there's just a lot more English written in the public domain
cues.zh: 一部分原因，是公開可取得的英文文字，比其他語言多得多，

cues.en: than other languages, but that's also a design choice by the language model developers.
cues.zh: 但這也是語言模型開發者的設計選擇。

cues.en: So regardless of the reasons, this has significant implications for the performance of models in different languages.
cues.zh: 不論原因，這對模型在不同語言的表現，都有重大影響。

cues.en: So if you speak languages other than English, you might have already noticed that commercial language
cues.zh: 如果你會英文以外的語言，可能已注意到，ChatGPT 這類商用語言

cues.en: models like ChatGPT are just not quite as fluent in non-English languages compared to English.
cues.zh: 模型，使用其他語言時，不如英文流暢。

cues.en: Now, in part, this reflects the model training set and how the model weights are tuned.
cues.zh: 一部分反映訓練資料集，以及模型權重的調整方式。

cues.en: But what I want to highlight in this video is that differences between model performance for different
cues.zh: 但這支影片想強調，不同語言的模型表現差異，

cues.en: languages already starts at the tokenizer, before the data even get into the model.
cues.zh: 在資料進入模型之前，從 tokenizer 就已開始。

cues.en: I'm going to illustrate this with a simple demo.
cues.zh: 用一個簡單示範說明。

cues.en: So I wrote this sentence here about blue towels.
cues.zh: 我寫了這個關於藍色毛巾的句子。

cues.en: And then I used Google Translate to translate this sentence into a half dozen other languages.
cues.zh: 再用 Google 翻譯，將它翻成大約六種其他語言。

cues.en: And then I tokenized these sentences and counted the number of tokens using GPT four and using Bert
cues.zh: 接著，對這些多語言句子斷詞，分別用 GPT-4 與 BERT，

cues.en: for this sentence, translated into multiple languages.
cues.zh: 計算各種譯文的 token 數。

cues.en: So you're going to see that the results will look something like this.
cues.zh: 結果會像這樣。

cues.en: So here is a table with different languages and the number of characters in the sentence translated into these languages.
cues.zh: 表格列出不同語言，以及句子翻成各語言後的字元數。

cues.en: And then also the number of tokens with the Bert tokenizer and with the GPT four tokenizer.
cues.zh: 還有 BERT tokenizer 與 GPT-4 tokenizer 的 token 數。

cues.en: Now, in this case, it happened to be that Bert and GPT tokenizers both ended up with 26 tokens.
cues.zh: 這個例子裡，BERT 與 GPT 的斷詞結果，剛好都是 26 個 token。

cues.en: Now, I didn't actually check whether these tokens are matched, so whether they correspond to the same subwords.
cues.zh: 但我沒檢查它們是否配對，也就是是否對應相同子詞。

cues.en: That's something you could check if you're curious.
cues.zh: 如果好奇，可以自行檢查。

cues.en: Anyway, let me now switch to Python and show you the rest of this table, and then we'll have a discussion about what these findings mean.
cues.zh: 現在切換到 Python，展示表格其餘部分，再討論這些發現的意義。

cues.en: Here I am installing and then importing the GPT and the Bert tokenizer.
cues.zh: 這裡安裝並匯入 GPT 與 BERT tokenizer。

cues.en: So we will differentiate them using G and b okay.
cues.zh: 用 g 與 b 區分。

cues.en: Here is the list of languages.
cues.zh: 這是語言清單。

cues.en: Here is the sentence that I wrote.
cues.zh: 這是我寫的句子：

cues.en: Blue tiles are great because they remind you of the sea.
cues.zh: 藍色毛巾很棒，因為讓你想到大海。

cues.en: Although the sea is wet and tiles work better when they are dry.
cues.zh: 不過，大海是濕的，而毛巾乾的時候更好用。

cues.en: Don't ask me where this stuff comes from.
cues.zh: 別問我，這些句子是怎麼想出來的。

cues.en: It doesn't matter.
cues.zh: 不重要。

cues.en: Okay, so then as I mentioned, I used Google Translate to go from this English sentence into Spanish and Arabic and Persian and so on for these other languages.
cues.zh: 如前所述，我用 Google 翻譯，將英文句子翻成西班牙文、阿拉伯文、波斯文等其他語言。

cues.en: Now, I have to admit, I am not fluent in any of these other languages.
cues.zh: 必須承認，我並不精通其中任何一種語言。

cues.en: So, uh, if you are familiar with these languages, you can, uh, read through them and see whether this translation is pretty good, whether it's accurate.
cues.zh: 如果你熟悉這些語言，可以讀讀，看看翻譯好不好、是否準確。

cues.en: But, uh, certainly for, you know, the point of this video, uh, I trust Google Translate enough
cues.zh: 不過，就這支影片的目的而言，我對 Google 翻譯的信任程度，

cues.en: that the main theme, the take home message here is going to be preserved regardless of the accuracy of this translation.
cues.zh: 足以相信無論翻譯是否完全準確，主要訊息與重點仍會保留。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So from here, the rest of this code is really simple.
cues.zh: 之後的程式很簡單。

cues.en: All I'm doing is looping over all of the sentences, and I'm zipping them up just so I can get the,
cues.zh: 走訪所有句子，並用 zip 配對，方便同時取得

cues.en: uh, name of the language and the text of the language tokenizing.
cues.zh: 語言名稱與該語言的文字，再進行斷詞。

cues.en: And, uh, in GPT tokenizing in Bert here you can see I'm excluding the two edge cases, the two special
cues.zh: 分別用 GPT 與 BERT 斷詞。可以看到，這裡排除了兩端的兩個特殊

cues.en: tokens that are added in the beginning and the end of the stream.
cues.zh: token，也就是文字串流開頭與結尾加入的 token。

cues.en: And then I'm just printing the results.
cues.zh: 接著印出結果。

cues.en: Okay, so here is what we find.
cues.zh: 這就是發現。

cues.en: So the number of characters is pretty similar for all of the languages except for Chinese.
cues.zh: 除了中文，其他語言的字元數相當接近。

cues.en: Chinese has fewer characters, and that's because Chinese characters can contain a lot of information within one character.
cues.zh: 中文的字元較少，因為一個中文字，就能包含很多資訊。

cues.en: It's a morpheme based written language.
cues.zh: 它是以語素為基礎的書寫語言。

cues.en: Here we see for Bert, and this also varies quite a bit.
cues.zh: 這裡是 BERT，差異也相當大。

cues.en: We go from 26 tokens in English up to almost 100 tokens in Arabic and Persian.
cues.zh: 從英文的 26 個 token，到阿拉伯文與波斯文接近 100 個。

cues.en: And I'm also not an expert on these languages, but I do understand or am familiar with the idea that the written language is the same.
cues.zh: 我不是這些語言的專家，但知道它們的書寫系統相同，

cues.en: So the letters are the same, but the languages are different.
cues.zh: 也就是字母相同，但語言不同。

cues.en: But anyway, here is something that is really striking to me.
cues.zh: 不過，有件事讓我很驚訝。

cues.en: When we look in Tamil Tomorrow we get 150 characters.
cues.zh: 看泰米爾文，有 150 個字元。

cues.en: Okay, so that already is the most number of characters out of this set of languages.
cues.zh: 這已經是這組語言中，字元數最多的。

cues.en: But in Bert, that ends up being 35 tokens, and in GPT it's a whopping 200 tokens.
cues.zh: 但 BERT 得到 35 個 token，GPT 卻多達 200 個。

cues.en: That's like an order of magnitude more tokens than in English.
cues.zh: 大約比英文多一個數量級。

cues.en: It's also crazy enough, more tokens than characters.
cues.zh: 更驚人的是，token 數竟然比字元數還多。

cues.en: And to a lesser extreme, you see a similar phenomenon in Chinese.
cues.zh: 中文也有類似現象，只是沒那麼極端。

cues.en: So there are 55 tokens for 39 characters.
cues.zh: 39 個字元，卻有 55 個 token。

cues.en: So this completely flies in the face of my claim in the previous video that tokenization is compression.
cues.zh: 這完全違背上一支影片「斷詞就是壓縮」的說法。

cues.en: Here we are actually expanding the text, so we need more tokens to represent this text compared to the number of characters.
cues.zh: 這裡其實把文字展開了，表示文字所需的 token，比字元數還多。

cues.en: So that was quite interesting.
cues.zh: 這很有意思。

cues.en: We saw that tokenization definitely does not trivially equal compression in all cases.
cues.zh: 可以看到，斷詞並不是在所有情況下，都必然等於壓縮。

cues.en: Now, to be clear, this that statement that claim very often is the case, especially in, uh, English
cues.zh: 說清楚一點，這個說法經常成立，尤其是英文，

cues.en: and other languages that these models have been trained extensively on.
cues.zh: 以及這些模型接受大量訓練的其他語言。

cues.en: And as I mentioned in the previous video, the primary goal of a tokenizer is to make text more efficient for processing by a language model.
cues.zh: 如上一支影片所說，tokenizer 的主要目標，是讓語言模型更有效率地處理文字。

cues.en: Compression can be part of that goal of efficiency, but it's not necessarily the case.
cues.zh: 壓縮可能是效率目標的一部分，但不一定如此。

cues.en: Chinese is a particularly interesting illustration of this, because a single character in Chinese can refer to a word, or even several words in English.
cues.zh: 中文是很有趣的例子，因為單一中文字，可能對應英文的一個，甚至好幾個單字。

cues.en: Of course, another reason for this expansion of tokens instead of compression is that languages like
cues.zh: token 展開、而非壓縮的另一個原因，是

cues.en: Chinese and also Tamil are just less represented in the training set for tokenizers and language models.
cues.zh: 中文與泰米爾文，在 tokenizer 與語言模型訓練集中所佔比例較低。

cues.en: In other words, it's not that there's something intrinsic to Tamil that necessitates a higher token count.
cues.zh: 換句話說，不是泰米爾文有什麼內在特性，必然需要更多 token。

cues.en: That's just a result of insufficient training data.
cues.zh: 這只是訓練資料不足的結果。

cues.en: Now, from a cultural or usage perspective, we might find that unfortunate.
cues.zh: 從文化或使用角度，可能覺得可惜。

cues.en: But from a commercial perspective, it is understandable if OpenAI has relatively few users who are
cues.zh: 但從商業角度，可以理解：如果 OpenAI 使用者中，

cues.en: interacting with GPT in Tamil, then it doesn't really make sense for them to put enormous resources into optimizing the model for a language that is infrequently used.
cues.zh: 只有少數人用泰米爾文與 GPT 互動，就不太有理由投入龐大資源，最佳化這個較少使用的語言。

cues.en: And the last thing that I want to say here is to keep in mind that this video is just a quick demo, with literally one sentence translated into only a handful of languages.
cues.zh: 最後，記得這支影片只是一個快速示範，真的只用一個句子，翻成少數幾種語言。

cues.en: So what I stated here really is true, but if you really want to understand tokenizer behavior and differences
cues.zh: 這裡提出的概念確實成立，但若真的想理解 tokenizer 的行為，以及不同

cues.en: across different languages, you really need to study this more rigorously and with a lot more data.
cues.zh: 語言之間的差異，必須使用更多資料，更嚴謹地研究。
